title: At Most One Swap to Match
statement:
You get two strings a and b of the same length. You may pick one of the two strings and swap two of its letters, or you may do nothing.

Return true if the two strings can be made equal this way, and false otherwise.

examples.why: Swapping the l and the n in "plane" gives "pnale". Only positions 1 and 3 differ, and their letters are crossed.
They are already equal, and doing nothing is allowed.
Same letters, but all three positions differ. One swap fixes at most two.

constraints: Both strings have only lowercase English letters
hints: One swap changes exactly two positions. How many positions may differ between a and b?
Zero differing positions is fine. One is never fixable. Two might be. Three or more never are.
With exactly two differing positions i and j, check that a[i] = b[j] and a[j] = b[i].

explain.intuition:
A swap touches two positions, so it can repair at most two mismatches. Walk both strings together and note where they differ. Zero mismatches: already equal. Exactly two mismatches at i and j: a swap fixes them only if the letters are crossed. Anything else: impossible.

Swapping in a or in b gives the same condition, so you never need to try both.
steps: Collect the indexes where a[i] !== b[i]; stop early if there are more than two.
If there are exactly two, i and j, return a[i] === b[j] && a[j] === b[i].
pitfalls: Comparing letter counts only. "abc" and "bca" have the same letters but need two swaps.
Accepting any two mismatches without checking that the letters cross. "ab" vs "cd" differs in two places, but no swap fixes it.
Returning true for exactly one mismatch. A swap always moves two letters, so a single wrong letter can never be fixed.

solutions.title: Try every swap
solutions.idea: If the strings are equal, done. Otherwise try every swap in a and compare with b.

solutions.title: Track the mismatches
solutions.idea: Zero mismatches, or exactly two that cross.

followups: Allow up to two swaps, all in the same string. How many mismatches can you now fix, and what must you check?
Given many strings, group together all strings that are one swap (or zero) away from each other.
lcTitle: Check if One String Swap Can Make Strings Equal
